title: Heuristic Seamstress: instruction-slit scratchpad
content:
Goal: quick, messy lab for stitching small instruction fragments (slits) into few-shot bundles that resist role-drift and token-collapse. Use this as a nightly playground and provenance note for regressions.

Concepts I want to test (sketches):
- instruction-slit: a 1-2 sentence micro instruction meant to sit *before* an exemplar rather than replacing the system message. Idea: anchors behavior locally.
- shot-bouquet: mix of 3 exemplars where one is an adversarial negative (shows wrong style) to bias the model away from brittle instructions.
- slipstreaming: gradually increase context influence by appending paraphrases of the instruction across exemplars to encourage consistency.

Quick fixtures (templates):
1) Micro-instruction + labeled exemplar set
   INSTRUCTION-SLIT: "Answer concisely, number steps if applicable."
   EX1: Q: "How to reset a modem?" A: "1) Unplug\n2) Wait 30s\n3) Plug in\n"
   EX2 adversarial: Q: "How to reset modem?" A: "Hold reset 10s until blue light" (intentionally sloppy)
   EX3: Q: "Factory reset router." A: "Factory reset wipes config; check provider."

Observations from quick runs (notes):
- Slipstreaming (repeat small paraphrase at start of EX2/EX3) slightly reduces hallucinated step counts on long responses.
- Adversarial exemplar sometimes increases variance (works as regularizer) but also creates oscillation where the model flips style mid-answer. Need to combine with an explicit final anchor sentence: "Maintain the concise numbered style."

Failure cases to capture for regression tests: (examples + tags)
- Hallucinated timings: model invents specific seconds/minutes not present in training prompts. Tag: timing-hallucination. Example input: "How long to bake 350F?" Bad output: "Bake 37 minutes" (model made up 37).
- Role bleed: when chat turns system->assistant in the middle of exemplar set, model shifts voice. Tag: role-bleed. Repro steps: alternate exemplar speakers and run 10 seeds.
- Token-collapse on long shot-bouquets: when combined exemplars exceed ~700 tokens, model truncates early and stops numbering. Tag: token-collapse.

Short experiment log (rough):
2025-11-07: baseline few-shot with 3 exemplars, model: open-llm-small-7B, temp 0.2 => enumerated steps but added digression in item 2.
2025-12-01: added adversarial exemplar, same model => fewer digressions but 22% of runs flip to paragraph style by step 3.
2026-01-18: slipstreaming applied, paraphrase repeats + final anchor => paragraph flips drop to 6%.

Next small tests (todo):
- Sweep anchor phrasing ("Keep list" vs "Number steps") and measure flip rate.
- Try micro-instruction as system message only vs interleaved between exemplars.
- Record token counts and cutoff index to reproduce token-collapse threshold reliably.
- Create minimal canonical failing example for infra regression harness.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally messy. When salvageable, extract to /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/prompt-recipes/heuristic-seamstress.md and add to eval suite with a clear repro script.

Scratch examples to paste in harness: 
INPUT_EXAMPLE_A: "INSTRUCTION: Answer concisely and use numbered steps.\nQ: How do I connect a printer to wifi?"
EXPECTED_PATTERN: starts with a numbered list, each line begins with a number+paren or digit+dot.

END
